title: LazyVM settings
description: Every LazyVM setting, with its default. List only the settings you want to change: in LazyVM.Settings.json for every VM on this host, or in a VM's VM.json for that VM alone. Hover a setting's name to see what it does.

Proxy.description: The proxy the step runs as; empty for the Agent service account. Its credential is not recorded.

$schema.description: Points your editor at this schema, for autocomplete and checking. Leave it as it is.

DiskDir.description: Where the VM's Windows disk and answer-file disc are kept. Hyper-V keeps checkpoint disks (.avhdx) beside the disks they belong to. A path inside the LazyVM folder (like 'Shared\ISO') or a full path on another drive (like 'E:\VMs'). {VM} is replaced by the VM's name.

OSDiskSizeGB.description: Size of the Windows disk in GB. It grows as needed up to this size.

MemStartGB.description: Memory the VM starts with, in GB. 8 is Microsoft's minimum for a Dev Drive; dynamic memory releases it when the VM is idle.

MemMinGB.description: The least memory dynamic memory may shrink the VM to, in GB.

MemMaxGB.description: The most memory dynamic memory may give the VM, in GB.

EnableEnhancedSession.description: Use Enhanced Session Mode in VMConnect: clipboard, drive and audio redirection over the VMBus, with no network setup.

SwitchName.description: The Hyper-V virtual switch the VM connects to. 'Default Switch' gives NAT and DHCP automatically.

NatSwitchName.description: Fallback only: if SwitchName does not exist, an internal switch with this name is created, with NAT.

NatSubnet.description: Fallback only: the NAT network for NatSwitchName.

NatHostIP.description: Fallback only: the host's address on the NAT network.

ISOPath.description: The Windows 11 Enterprise evaluation ISO. If it is not found here, the ISO folder is searched for one. A path inside the LazyVM folder (like 'Shared\ISO') or a full path on another drive (like 'E:\VMs'). {VM} is replaced by the VM's name.

ISOMinSizeGB.description: An ISO smaller than this, in GB, is treated as a failed download.

ISOSearchRoot.description: The folder searched for a Windows ISO when ISOPath does not exist. A path inside the LazyVM folder (like 'Shared\ISO') or a full path on another drive (like 'E:\VMs'). {VM} is replaced by the VM's name.

ISODownloadPage.description: Where to download the Windows 11 Enterprise evaluation. Opened for you when no ISO is found.

SQLIsoPath.description: The SQL Server installation ISO. Downloaded from SQLIsoUrl when missing. A path inside the LazyVM folder (like 'Shared\ISO') or a full path on another drive (like 'E:\VMs'). {VM} is replaced by the VM's name.

SQLIsoUrl.description: Where the SQL Server ISO is downloaded from: the SQL Server 2025 Enterprise Developer ISO, from which LazyVM installs the Standard Developer edition, free for development and test, so code cannot come to depend on Enterprise-only features.

SQLDiskPath.description: The SQL data disk. It is never deleted by a rebuild, so databases survive one. A path inside the LazyVM folder (like 'Shared\ISO') or a full path on another drive (like 'E:\VMs'). {VM} is replaced by the VM's name.

SQLDiskSizeGB.description: Size of the SQL data disk in GB. It grows as needed up to this size.

SQLDiskGuid.description: Recorded by LazyVM: the SQL data disk's GPT disk GUID inside the VM, written the first time the VM prepares the disk. It is the first thing LazyVM looks for to find the disk. Leave it as it is; a VM copied with -From starts without it.

SQLDiskScsiLocation.description: Recorded by LazyVM: the location on the VM's SCSI controller 0 where the SQL data disk was attached. It is how a new, empty disk is found. Leave it as it is; a VM copied with -From starts without it.

MoveSqlDataToDataDisk.description: Move an existing SQL Server instance's user databases and tempdb onto the data disk. Files are copied and checked before the originals go. master, model and msdb are never moved.

SQLInstallMinutes.description: How long the SQL Server install may take before it is treated as failed, in minutes.

UseDevDrive.description: Give the VM a Dev Drive: a ReFS volume with Defender performance mode, for source code and builds. It is never deleted by a rebuild.

DevDrivePath.description: The Dev Drive disk on the host. Keep it here, not inside the VM: a rebuild replaces the VM's own disks. A path inside the LazyVM folder (like 'Shared\ISO') or a full path on another drive (like 'E:\VMs'). {VM} is replaced by the VM's name.

DevDriveSizeGB.description: Size of the Dev Drive in GB. Dev Drive needs at least 50.

DevDriveLetter.description: The Dev Drive's letter inside the VM.

DevDriveFilters.description: Extra file system filters allowed on the Dev Drive. Everything except antivirus is detached by default, which is where the speed comes from. 'PrjFlt' for Live Unit Testing, 'WinSetupMon' if TEMP is on the drive, 'bindFlt' and 'wcifs' for containers.

DevDriveGuid.description: Recorded by LazyVM: the Dev Drive disk's GPT disk GUID inside the VM, written the first time the VM prepares the disk. It is the first thing LazyVM looks for to find the disk. Leave it as it is; a VM copied with -From starts without it.

DevDriveScsiLocation.description: Recorded by LazyVM: the location on the VM's SCSI controller 0 where the Dev Drive disk was attached. It is how a new, empty disk is found. Leave it as it is; a VM copied with -From starts without it.

UserDiskPath.description: The User disk: Documents, Desktop, Downloads, .ssh and source\repos live on it, so a rebuild never touches them. A path inside the LazyVM folder (like 'Shared\ISO') or a full path on another drive (like 'E:\VMs'). {VM} is replaced by the VM's name.

UserDiskSizeGB.description: Size of the User disk in GB. It grows as needed up to this size.

UserDiskLetter.description: Preferred letter for the User disk inside the VM. If it is taken, another is chosen.

UserDiskGuid.description: Recorded by LazyVM: the User disk's GPT disk GUID inside the VM, written the first time the VM prepares the disk. It is the first thing LazyVM looks for to find the disk. Leave it as it is; a VM copied with -From starts without it.

UserDiskScsiLocation.description: Recorded by LazyVM: the location on the VM's SCSI controller 0 where the User disk was attached. It is how a new, empty disk is found. Leave it as it is; a VM copied with -From starts without it.

CheckpointDir.description: Where Hyper-V checkpoints of the VM are kept. A path inside the LazyVM folder (like 'Shared\ISO') or a full path on another drive (like 'E:\VMs'). {VM} is replaced by the VM's name.

VSSettingsBackup.description: Where the Visual Studio settings export is kept between rebuilds. A path inside the LazyVM folder (like 'Shared\ISO') or a full path on another drive (like 'E:\VMs'). {VM} is replaced by the VM's name.

LogFile.description: The VM's log file. A path inside the LazyVM folder (like 'Shared\ISO') or a full path on another drive (like 'E:\VMs'). {VM} is replaced by the VM's name.

LogMaxSizeMB.description: When the log is bigger than this, in MB, it is set aside and a new one started.

CredStoreDir.description: Where the key that encrypts every VM's stored passwords is kept. The encrypted passwords themselves are in each VM's Credentials folder. A path inside the LazyVM folder (like 'Shared\ISO') or a full path on another drive (like 'E:\VMs'). {VM} is replaced by the VM's name.

StateDir.description: Where the guest's captured state (databases, settings, files) is kept for a rebuild. A path inside the LazyVM folder (like 'Shared\ISO') or a full path on another drive (like 'E:\VMs'). {VM} is replaced by the VM's name.

GuestAdminUser.description: The VM's administrator account, when none has been stored with Set-LazyVMCredential.

GuestComputerName.description: The VM's computer name. {VM} is replaced by the VM's name.

GuestTimeZone.description: The VM's time zone, as Windows names it (Get-TimeZone -ListAvailable).

GuestRemoveApps.description: Built-in Windows apps removed from the VM at every build, for every user and for users created later. Package names as Get-AppxPackage shows them; * is a wildcard. Your list replaces the default, so copy it and add to it.

GuestRemoveOneDrive.description: Remove OneDrive from the VM at every build, and stop it from installing for new users.

GuestDarkMode.description: Use the dark theme in the VM, for every user.

GuestShowFileExtensions.description: Show file extensions in File Explorer in the VM, for every user.

GuestTaskbarLeft.description: Put the Start button and taskbar icons on the left in the VM, for every user.

GuestHideWidgets.description: Turn off Widgets in the VM.

GuestHideTaskbarSearch.description: Hide the search box on the taskbar in the VM, for every user. Search still works from the Start menu.

GuestSetupDir.description: A working folder inside the VM for installers and captured files.

GuestDataDriveLetter.description: Preferred letter for the SQL data disk inside the VM. If it is taken, another is chosen and every SQL path follows it.

SqlDataFolder.description: Folder on the SQL data disk for database files.

SqlLogFolder.description: Folder on the SQL data disk for transaction logs.

SqlTempFolder.description: No longer used: tempdb stays in SQL Server's own folder on C:, since it is recreated at every start. Kept so older VM.json files still load; it can be deleted.

SqlBackupFolder.description: Folder on the SQL data disk for backups.

GuestWaitMinutes.description: How long to wait for Windows to install and reach the desktop, in minutes.

GuestNetworkWaitMinutes.description: How long to wait for the VM's network before downloads, in minutes.

VSInstallMinutes.description: How long each Visual Studio Installer product (Visual Studio, SSMS) may take to install, in minutes.

UnsignedExtensions.description: Marketplace extensions, by item name (Publisher.Name, as in the extension's Marketplace link), that the Visual Studio Installer may install even though they are not signed. Unsigned extensions are refused unless listed here.

InstallerBootstrappers.description: The Visual Studio Installer bootstrapper for each channel a tooling list uses. {edition} becomes the edition in lower case, so Microsoft.VisualStudio.Product.Community uses vs_community.exe. Listing this setting replaces the whole table, so copy it and add to it.

AppSettings.description: Application settings carried across a rebuild: each registry key is exported by a capture and imported by a restore, after the application has been reinstalled.

RegistryKey.description: The registry key to carry across, starting HKCU\ or HKLM\.

RebuildThresholdDays.description: How many days before the Windows evaluation expires the daily maintenance acts: it rearms if it can, and rebuilds only when it cannot.

DeleteRetiredDiskOnSuccess.description: Delete the old Windows disk once a rebuilt VM has been checked. false keeps every generation, which adds up fast.

GuestProjectPaths.description: No longer used: Documents, Desktop, Downloads, .ssh and source\repos are on the User disk, which a rebuild never touches (#137). Kept so older VM.json files still load; it can be deleted.

ProjectExcludeDirs.description: No longer used, since GuestProjectPaths is not captured. Kept so older VM.json files still load; it can be deleted.

MaxProjectCaptureGB.description: No longer used, since GuestProjectPaths is not captured. Kept so older VM.json files still load; it can be deleted.

GuestRestoreRoot.description: No longer used, since GuestProjectPaths is not captured. Kept so older VM.json files still load; it can be deleted.

ToolingCheckpointsToKeep.description: How many tooling checkpoints to keep. Older ones are removed.

ToolingHistoryDays.description: No longer used: LazyVM no longer keeps a daily copy of the tooling list. Every recorded version is in History with the rest of VM.json. Kept so older VM.json files still load; it can be deleted.

ToolingWingetExclude.description: winget packages never recorded in the tooling list: ones that come with Windows, and products the Visual Studio Installer manages. Wildcards allowed. Listing this setting replaces the whole list, so copy it and add to it.

ToolingWingetCheck.description: winget ids to check for directly, for packages winget can match but leaves out of its export.

Tooling.description: The VM's tooling list: Visual Studio Installer products with their components and extensions, winget packages, and other programs, without versions. A build installs it, and maintenance records what you install or remove inside the VM. A new VM starts with the list in the module's Data\Tooling.Default.json.

Version.description: The format of the list. Leave it as it is.

Products.description: Visual Studio Installer products: Visual Studio, SSMS.

Programs.description: Other installed programs, by name without version.

AwaitingReinstall.description: Items from before the last rebuild that must be installed by hand. Delete one you no longer want.

GuestEnvironment.description: The guest's own Windows environment, recorded by LazyVM whenever it changes and put back by a rebuild: the environment variables you set, PATH entries, hosts file entries and mapped drives. A variable whose name looks secret (a token, key, password or connection string) is listed here by name only; its value is kept encrypted in <Name>\Credentials\environment.cred. Empty until first recorded.

MachineVariables.description: System environment variables, other than those Windows sets itself.

UserVariables.description: The guest account's own environment variables, other than those Windows sets itself.

SecretVariables.description: Variables whose values are kept encrypted, not here.

MachinePath.description: The system PATH, in order. A rebuild adds the entries a fresh install lacks.

UserPath.description: The guest account's PATH, in order. A rebuild adds the entries a fresh install lacks.

Hosts.description: The active lines of the hosts file.

MappedDrives.description: The guest account's mapped network drives.

GuestFirewallRules.description: The firewall rules added in the guest, recorded by LazyVM whenever they change and put back by a rebuild. Windows' own rules and LazyVM's are left out. Empty until first recorded.

Protocol.description: TCP, UDP, Any or a protocol number.

LocalPort.description: Ports or ranges, like 5000 or 8000-8010; Any for every port.

RemoteAddress.description: Addresses, subnets or ranges; Any for every address.

Profile.description: Any, or the network profiles it applies to, like 'Domain, Private'.

GuestScheduledTasks.description: The scheduled tasks created in the guest's root task folder, recorded by LazyVM whenever they change and put back by a rebuild. LazyVM's own tasks are left out. Empty until first recorded.

Xml.description: The task as Export-ScheduledTask writes it.

GuestAppSettings.description: The values under each AppSettings registry key in the guest, recorded by LazyVM whenever they change and put back by a rebuild. A value whose name looks secret is listed by name only; its data is kept encrypted in Credentials\appsettings.cred. Empty until first recorded.

Path.description: The subkey under RegistryKey, empty for the key itself.

Name.description: The value's name, empty for the key's default value.

Data.description: Binary data is Base64; a MultiString is a list of strings.

GuestSql.description: The guest's SQL Server logins, their server roles, the instance settings and the SQL Agent jobs, operators and alerts, recorded by LazyVM whenever they change and put back by a rebuild. A SQL login keeps its SID and password hash, never the password, so database users are not orphaned. Empty until first recorded.

Configs.description: Instance settings (sp_configure) that are not zero or are waiting for a restart.

Logins.description: Logins other than sa and those SQL Server and Windows create themselves.

SidHex.description: The login's SID, kept so database users stay linked to it.

HashHex.description: A SQL login's password hash; empty for a Windows login.

Databases.description: The user databases and their data and log files on the SQL data disk, which a rebuild attaches to the new instance. Recorded from #132 on.

Files.description: In file order: the primary data file first.

Agent.description: SQL Server Agent operators, jobs (with their steps and schedules) and alerts (with whom they notify). They live in msdb, which a rebuild replaces.

MaintenanceTime.description: When the VM's daily maintenance runs, 24-hour time on the host. New-LazyVM sets each new VM an hour after the latest existing one.
